activities.name: Trinity College & Book of Kells
activities.description: See the illuminated 9th-century manuscript and the stunning Long Room library with 200,000 ancient books.
activities.tips: Book the earliest morning slot to avoid crowds. The Long Room is the highlight.

activities.name: Kilmainham Gaol
activities.description: Powerful guided tour of the historic prison where leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were executed. Deeply moving.
activities.tips: Book weeks ahead — this sells out fast. One of the most impactful historical sites in Ireland.

activities.name: Howth Cliff Walk
activities.description: Take the DART train 30 min to the fishing village of Howth. Walk the cliff loop trail with stunning Irish Sea views.
activities.tips: The loop trail is ~6km and moderate difficulty. Bring a rain jacket even if it looks sunny.

activities.name: Chester Beatty Library
activities.description: Free museum with extraordinary collection of manuscripts, prints, and art from Asia, Middle East, and Europe. Named European Museum of the Year.
activities.tips: Don't skip the rooftop garden. The Islamic collection is particularly stunning.

activities.name: Guinness Storehouse
activities.description: Seven floors telling the story of Guinness. Ends with a pint at the Gravity Bar with 360-degree views of Dublin.
activities.tips: Book online for discounts. The view from the top alone is worth it even if you're not a beer person.

activities.name: St Stephen's Green
activities.description: Beautiful Victorian park in the heart of Dublin. Perfect for a jet-lag stroll.
activities.tips: Enter from the Grafton Street arch for the best first impression.

activities.name: Merrion Square & Georgian Dublin
activities.description: Stroll past colorful Georgian doors and Oscar Wilde's childhood home. The park has a wonderful Wilde statue.
activities.tips: Look for the famous colored doors along the north and east sides of the square.

activities.name: Teeling Whiskey Distillery
activities.description: Dublin's first new distillery in 125 years. Excellent tour with tastings in the Liberties neighborhood.
activities.tips: The premium tasting tour is worth the upgrade if you're whiskey fans.

activities.name: Irish Rail: Dublin → Galway
activities.description: Scenic train from Dublin Heuston to Galway Ceannt station. Runs roughly hourly.
activities.tips: Book online for cheaper fares. Sit on the right side for better views after Athlone.

activities.name: Latin Quarter & Spanish Arch
activities.description: Wander Galway's medieval Latin Quarter — cobblestone streets, colorful shopfronts, buskers, and the 16th-century Spanish Arch by the river.
activities.tips: Shop Street and Quay Street are the main pedestrian arteries. Great for people-watching.

activities.name: Traditional Music Session
activities.description: Galway is Ireland's trad music capital. Catch a live session at Tigh Neachtain, The Crane Bar, or Monroe's Tavern.
activities.tips: Sessions usually start around 9-9:30pm. Arrive early for a seat. Tigh Neachtain is the most atmospheric.

activities.name: Cliffs of Moher & Burren Day Tour
activities.description: Small-group day tour from Galway to the iconic Cliffs of Moher (214m sea cliffs) and the Burren's lunar limestone landscape.
activities.tips: Book a small-group tour (max 16) for a better experience. Galway Tour Company and Paddywagon both well-rated. Bring warm layers — it's windy at the cliffs even in July.

activities.name: Connemara Day Tour
activities.description: Explore Connemara's wild beauty: mountains, bogs, Kylemore Abbey, and the rugged coast. Less touristy than the Cliffs.
activities.tips: Good alternative to a second nature day if weather looks good. Kylemore Abbey alone is worth it.

activities.name: Aran Islands Day Trip
activities.description: Ferry to Inis Mór, the largest Aran Island. Rent bikes, visit the ancient cliff fort Dún Aonghasa, see traditional Irish culture.
activities.tips: Very weather-dependent — check forecast. If rough seas, choose Connemara instead. Ferry is 40 min from Rossaveal.

activities.name: Walk the Royal Mile
activities.description: Edinburgh's famous mile-long street connecting the Castle to Holyrood Palace. Explore the historic closes (alleyways) branching off it.
activities.tips: Duck into the closes — Mary King's Close and Advocate's Close are especially atmospheric.

activities.name: Edinburgh Castle
activities.description: Scotland's most visited attraction, perched on Castle Rock. See the Crown Jewels, Stone of Destiny, and stunning city views.
activities.tips: Book a morning slot. Don't miss the One O'Clock Gun firing (Mon-Sat) — it's a tradition since 1861.

activities.name: St Giles' Cathedral
activities.description: Stunning Gothic cathedral on the Royal Mile. The Thistle Chapel's intricate carvings are breathtaking.
activities.tips: Free to enter but donation appreciated. The Thistle Chapel is tiny — don't walk past it.

activities.name: National Museum of Scotland
activities.description: World-class free museum with everything from Dolly the Sheep to ancient Scottish artifacts. The Grand Gallery architecture alone is worth visiting.
activities.tips: Head to the rooftop terrace for a great view of the castle. The Scottish history galleries on levels 0-3 are the highlight.

activities.name: Arthur's Seat Hike
activities.description: Hike the ancient volcano in the heart of Edinburgh (251m). Spectacular 360-degree views of the city, castle, and Firth of Forth.
activities.tips: Start from Holyrood Palace. The main path is well-trodden. Save this for clear weather — the views make it.

activities.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
activities.description: Interactive tour at the top of the Royal Mile, right next to the Castle. Barrel ride, tasting, and the world's largest Scotch whisky collection.
activities.tips: The Silver Tour is good value. Gold/Platinum include more tastings.

activities.name: 2-Day Highlands & Loch Ness Tour (Rabbie's)
activities.description: Small-group tour (max 16) in a Mercedes mini-coach. Day 1: Cairngorms, Loch Morlich, Inverness. Day 2: Loch Ness, Glencoe, Great Glen, return to Edinburgh ~7pm. Overnight in a Highland B&B/guesthouse.
activities.tips: 30% off select July departures. Leave main luggage at Edinburgh hotel, bring overnight bag. Meals NOT included. Book 4-6 weeks ahead for July.

activities.name: Bus: Galway → Dublin Airport
activities.description: Direct bus from Galway to Dublin Airport. Citylink and GoBus both run this route multiple times daily. No need to go into Dublin city.
activities.tips: Book online for best price. Citylink and GoBus depart from Galway Coach Station (near Eyre Square). Allow 4+ hours before your flight. There is no train to the airport.

activities.name: Bus: Galway → Shannon Airport (alternative)
activities.description: Bus Eireann route from Galway to Shannon Airport. Shorter trip but fewer flight options from Shannon to Edinburgh.
activities.tips: Only useful if you find a good Shannon→Edinburgh flight (Ryanair runs this route but not daily). Dublin Airport has many more options.

activities.name: Dublin DART Train (day pass)
activities.description: The DART coastal train connects Dublin city to Howth (north) and Bray (south). Buy a Leap Card at any station for tap-on/tap-off convenience.
activities.tips: Get a Leap Visitor Card at the airport on arrival — covers DART, buses, and Luas tram for 1/3/7 days.

activities.name: Dublin Food Tour
activities.description: Guided walking food tour through Dublin's best independent food spots. Tastings at 6-7 stops including cheese, charcuterie, chocolate, and craft beer.
activities.tips: Fab Food Trails is the best-rated operator. Morning tours recommended — you'll be too full for lunch.

activities.name: Galway Food Tour
activities.description: Walk through Galway's food scene with a local guide. Visit the Galway Market (Saturdays), artisan producers, and hidden gems.
activities.tips: Saturday morning tour is best because the famous Galway Market is open. Galway's food scene punches way above its weight.

activities.name: Galway Market
activities.description: Vibrant weekend market at St Nicholas' Church. Local produce, street food, crafts, buskers. One of Ireland's best markets.
activities.tips: Open Saturday and Sunday. Go hungry — the street food is incredible. Try the crepes, oysters, and organic coffee.

activities.name: Calton Hill
activities.description: Easy hilltop walk with panoramic views of Edinburgh, the castle, Arthur's Seat, and the Firth of Forth. The National Monument (unfinished Parthenon replica) is here.
activities.tips: Best at sunset. Much easier than Arthur's Seat but equally rewarding views. 5-minute walk from Princes Street.

activities.name: Edinburgh Food Tour
activities.description: Walking food tour through Edinburgh's Old Town and beyond. Scottish cheese, whisky, haggis, craft beer, and chocolate tastings.
activities.tips: Eat Walk Edinburgh is the top-rated operator. They also do evening tours with whisky pairings.

activities.name: Phoenix Park
activities.description: One of Europe's largest enclosed city parks. Home to wild deer, the Dublin Zoo, and the US Ambassador's residence. Beautiful for walking or cycling.
activities.tips: Rent a bike near the park entrance to cover more ground. The deer herd is usually near the Papal Cross.

activities.name: Palestine Museum Scotland
activities.description: Europe's first and only Palestinian museum, opened May 2025 at 13a Dundas Street. Features paintings, sculptures, documentary films, and a striking floor map of 1948 Palestine. Works by Samia Halaby, Nabil Anani, and artists from Gaza.
activities.tips: Open Wed-Sun 11am-6pm. Small (3 rooms) but powerful. Volunteer-run, free entry. Sister institution to the Palestine Museum US in Connecticut.

activities.name: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
activities.description: Award-winning interactive museum in the Docklands telling the story of 10 million Irish emigrants and their impact on the world. Beautifully designed multimedia exhibits.
activities.tips: Won Europe's Leading Tourist Attraction. In the CHQ Building near the IFSC — combine with a Docklands walk.

activities.name: Dean Village Walk
activities.description: Hidden gem just minutes from Princes Street. A picturesque former milling village along the Water of Leith with stone cottages, a riverside path, and zero crowds.
activities.tips: Walk down from the Dean Bridge for the iconic view. Continue along the Water of Leith Walkway toward Stockbridge for coffee.

activities.name: Roe & Co Distillery
activities.description: Stunning distillery in the beautifully restored Guinness Power House building. Cocktail-focused experience — you blend your own whiskey and make cocktails rather than a traditional tasting tour.
activities.tips: More modern/interactive than Teeling. Great if you prefer cocktails over straight whiskey. The building alone is worth seeing.

activities.name: Micil Distillery
activities.description: Galway's first legal distillery in over 100 years. Small-batch poitín and gin made from a family recipe dating back to 1848. Intimate tours with tastings.
activities.tips: The poitín (traditional Irish spirit) is unique — you won't find this anywhere else. Also does cocktail masterclasses if you want something more hands-on.

activities.name: Holyrood Distillery
activities.description: Edinburgh's first single malt whisky distillery in nearly 100 years, right next to Holyrood Palace. Beautiful modern space in a converted railway engine shed. Gin and whisky tours with tastings.
activities.tips: The whisky won't be fully mature yet (opened 2019) but they have excellent gin and new-make spirit. The building and process are fascinating. Combine with Arthur's Seat or Holyrood Palace.

restaurants.name: Etto
restaurants.description: Relaxed, excellent Italian-Irish spot on Merrion Row. Perfect first-night dinner after a long flight.
restaurants.tips: Small space — book ahead. The pasta dishes are standouts.

restaurants.name: The Woollen Mills
restaurants.description: Casual cafe overlooking the Ha'penny Bridge and River Liffey. Great for a relaxed lunch between sightseeing.
restaurants.tips: Window seats have the best views. Good coffee and cakes too.

restaurants.name: Chapter One
restaurants.description: Michelin-starred modern Irish cuisine in a beautiful Georgian basement. Tasting menu is exceptional. Special-night worthy.
restaurants.tips: Book well ahead. The pre-theatre menu is great value if timing works.

restaurants.name: Aqua Restaurant
restaurants.description: Seafood restaurant on Howth pier with harbor views. Perfect after the cliff walk.
restaurants.tips: Sit outside if weather allows. The seafood chowder is famous.

restaurants.name: The Winding Stair
restaurants.description: Beautiful restaurant above a bookshop, overlooking the Ha'penny Bridge. Seasonal Irish cooking at its best.
restaurants.tips: One of Dublin's best-loved restaurants. The building is a former bookshop — buy a book downstairs.

restaurants.name: Ard Bia at Nimmos
restaurants.description: Atmospheric restaurant in a medieval stone building by the Spanish Arch. Creative, seasonal menu with Middle Eastern influences.
restaurants.tips: Upstairs for dinner, downstairs cafe for lunch. Both are excellent.

restaurants.name: Kai
restaurants.description: Galway's best-loved restaurant. Tiny, seasonal, farm-to-table cooking. Everything is locally sourced.
restaurants.tips: Very small — book ahead. No website reservations, call directly. Worth the effort.

restaurants.name: Dela Restaurant
restaurants.description: Neighborhood bistro with creative European-Irish menu. Warm, relaxed atmosphere.
restaurants.tips: Great wine list. The early bird menu is excellent value.

restaurants.name: McDonagh's
restaurants.description: Galway institution since 1902. Best fish and chips in the west of Ireland. Takeaway or sit-down.
restaurants.tips: The takeaway side is cheaper and just as good. Try the fresh-off-the-boat fish of the day.

restaurants.name: The Devil's Advocate
restaurants.description: Hidden down a close off the Royal Mile, this is a cocktail bar meets Scottish restaurant. Atmospheric stone-walled space.
restaurants.tips: The cocktail list is as good as the food. Great first-night option.

restaurants.name: The Kitchin
restaurants.description: Tom Kitchin's Michelin-starred restaurant in Leith. 'From nature to plate' philosophy. One of Scotland's best.
restaurants.tips: Book weeks ahead. The tasting menu is the way to go. In Leith (short taxi from Old Town).

restaurants.name: Dishoom Edinburgh
restaurants.description: Beautiful Bombay-style cafe in a stunning Art Deco space on St Andrew Square. Incredible bacon naan rolls for brunch.
restaurants.tips: Walk-ins only for breakfast/brunch. Dinner reservations recommended. The black daal is legendary.

restaurants.name: Ondine
restaurants.description: Top-end sustainable seafood restaurant on the Royal Mile. Beautiful dining room with open kitchen.
restaurants.tips: The oyster bar is great for a casual visit. Lunch is better value than dinner.

restaurants.name: Pichet
restaurants.description: Chic French-Irish bistro on Trinity Street. Excellent wine list and a lively atmosphere. Great for a nice dinner without Michelin prices.
restaurants.tips: The rotisserie chicken is legendary. Good pre-theatre option too.

restaurants.name: Forno
restaurants.description: Excellent Neapolitan-style pizza in a casual setting. Consistently rated Dublin's best pizza.
restaurants.tips: No reservations — arrive early or be prepared to wait. Worth it.

restaurants.name: Aniar
restaurants.description: Galway's Michelin-starred restaurant. Hyper-local tasting menu using only wild and foraged ingredients from the west of Ireland.
restaurants.tips: Book well ahead. Tasting menu only. An unforgettable food experience if you're serious about Irish cuisine.

restaurants.name: Loam
restaurants.description: Former Michelin-starred restaurant with a Nordic-Irish approach. Multi-course tasting menu using local produce. Stunning.
restaurants.tips: If choosing between Aniar and Loam, Aniar is more experimental, Loam is more refined. Both are exceptional.

restaurants.name: Timberyard
restaurants.description: Set in a converted warehouse, Timberyard serves a seasonal tasting menu using Scottish produce. Industrial-chic space.
restaurants.tips: Great cocktails too. More relaxed than The Kitchin but equally impressive food.

restaurants.name: Oink
restaurants.description: Cult-favourite hog roast sandwich shop on the Royal Mile. Slow-roasted pork in fresh rolls with stuffing and crackling.
restaurants.tips: There are two locations on the Royal Mile. Quick, cheap, and absolutely delicious. Perfect lunch fuel.

restaurants.name: Whiski Bar & Restaurant
restaurants.description: Over 400 whiskies and solid Scottish cooking on the Royal Mile. Live Scottish music most evenings.
restaurants.tips: Try a whisky flight paired with food. Great atmosphere with live music. Ask the bar staff for whisky recommendations — they're passionate.

restaurants.name: The Long Hall
restaurants.description: Stunning Victorian pub dating to 1766. Wood-paneled walls, antique mirrors, ornate chandeliers. Widely considered one of the best pints of Guinness in Dublin.
restaurants.tips: On South Great George's Street. Small and gets packed — arrive early evening for the best experience. Don't miss the snug.

restaurants.name: Mulligan's of Poolbeg Street
restaurants.description: 250-year-old pub widely regarded as serving the best pint of Guinness in Dublin. No frills, no pretension — just a perfect pint in an authentic setting.
restaurants.tips: Cash preferred. No live music, no TVs — just conversation and Guinness the way it's meant to be. A Dublin institution.

restaurants.name: O'Donoghue's
restaurants.description: Where The Dubliners got their start. Live traditional Irish music most afternoons and evenings — fiddles, tin whistles, bodhráns. The real deal.
restaurants.tips: On Baggot Street. Sessions are spontaneous and authentic, not staged. The outdoor area is great in summer.

restaurants.name: Tigh Neachtain
restaurants.description: Galway's most atmospheric pub, opened 1894. Beautiful old wooden paneling, dark cozy corners, memorabilia from times past. Corner of Cross Street and Quay Street.
restaurants.tips: The front bar is tiny and magical. Spills out onto the street in summer. Trad sessions most nights. The pub Galway locals love most.

restaurants.name: The Crane Bar
restaurants.description: The best live trad music venue in Galway — live sessions 7 nights a week both upstairs and downstairs. Intimate, authentic, and beloved by musicians.
restaurants.tips: Upstairs is where the serious sessions happen. Arrive early for a seat. Walking distance from the Latin Quarter on Sea Road.

restaurants.name: The Bow Bar
restaurants.description: Legendary whisky bar on West Bow with over 300 single malts, excellent cask ales, and no-nonsense pub atmosphere. Consistently voted one of Scotland's best pubs.
restaurants.tips: Order a dram and ask the bartender for a recommendation — they know their stuff. Simple food menu of pies and soups. No music, no TV — just whisky and conversation.

restaurants.name: Bennets Bar
restaurants.description: Gorgeous Victorian pub on Leven Street with ornate mirrors, decorative tiles, carved wooden pillars, and a massive malt whisky lineup. Feels like stepping into the 1890s.
restaurants.tips: Near the King's Theatre. One of the best-preserved Victorian pub interiors in Edinburgh. The stained glass and tilework are incredible.

restaurants.name: Cold Town House
restaurants.description: Microbrewery and beer hall in Grassmarket with a rooftop terrace overlooking Edinburgh Castle. Fresh beer brewed on-site, wood-fired pizza, and one of the best views in the city.
restaurants.tips: The rooftop terrace is the main draw — come for sunset. Brewery tours available. Great craft beer selection beyond their own brews.
